hook.en: No amplifier treats all frequencies alike. Very low and very high notes get less gain. The *frequency response* curve shows exactly which band an amplifier handles well.

title.en: Draw the frequency response of an RC coupled amplifier
Explain the fall of gain at low and high frequencies

say.en: No amplifier treats all frequencies alike. Very low and very high notes get less gain. The frequency response curve shows exactly which band an amplifier handles well. In this lesson: Draw the frequency response of an RC coupled amplifier.
Explain the fall of gain at low and high frequencies.
Define cut-off frequencies and bandwidth.

title.en: Why the gain changes with frequency

body.en: The reactance of a capacitor is $X_C = 1/(2\pi f C)$. At low frequencies $X_C$ of the coupling capacitors is large, so part of the signal is dropped across them, and $C_E$ no longer bypasses $R_E$; the gain falls. In the mid band the coupling and bypass capacitors act as short circuits and the small junction capacitances act as open circuits, so the gain is flat. At high frequencies the transistor junction capacitances and wiring capacitance shunt the signal to ground and β itself falls, so the gain falls again.

points.en: Low f: coupling and bypass capacitors
High f: junction and stray capacitance, fall of β

narration.en: Gain falls at low frequency because of coupling and bypass capacitors, and at high frequency because of junction and stray capacitances. In between it is flat.
narration.kn: ಕಡಿಮೆ ಆವೃತ್ತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಜೋಡಣಾ ಮತ್ತು ಬೈಪಾಸ್ ಧಾರಕಗಳಿಂದ, ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಆವೃತ್ತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಸಂಧಿ ಮತ್ತು ತಂತಿ ಧಾರಕತೆಯಿಂದ ವರ್ಧನೆ ಕುಸಿಯುತ್ತದೆ. ಮಧ್ಯ ಪಟ್ಟಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ವರ್ಧನೆ ಸ್ಥಿರ.

say.en: On the board: the frequency response curve.

narration.en: At low frequencies the coupling capacitor (here in series with 2 kΩ) drops part of the signal, so fL = 1/(2π × 2 kΩ × C); at high frequencies stray and transistor capacitances cut the gain above fH. Between them is the flat mid band. The bandwidth is fH − fL, measured 3 dB down. Drag the marker to read the gain.

body.en: The lower *cut-off* $f_L$ and upper cut-off $f_H$ are the frequencies at which the gain falls to $A_m/\sqrt2 = 0.707A_m$, that is 3 dB below the mid-band gain. There the output power is half the mid-band power, so they are also called half-power points. The bandwidth is $BW = f_H - f_L$. For an audio amplifier $f_L$ is a few tens of hertz and $f_H$ about 20 kHz or more.

points.en: At fL and fH: A = 0.707 Am (−3 dB)
Output power is half: half-power points

narration.en: At the two cut-off frequencies the gain is 0.707 of its mid-band value, three decibels down. The bandwidth is fH minus fL.
narration.kn: ಎರಡು ಕಡಿತ ಆವೃತ್ತಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ವರ್ಧನೆ ಮಧ್ಯ ಮೌಲ್ಯದ 0.707 ಪಟ್ಟು, ಅಂದರೆ 3 dB ಕಡಿಮೆ. ಬ್ಯಾಂಡ್‌ವಿಡ್ತ್ = fH − fL.

problem.en: An amplifier has a mid-band gain of 120, fL = 40 Hz and fH = 20 kHz. Find the bandwidth and the gain at the cut-off frequencies (as a number and in dB).

steps.en: Mid-band gain = 20 log 120 = 41.6 dB, so the cut-off gain is 38.6 dB (3 dB less).

narration.en: Let us work this out together. An amplifier has a mid-band gain of 120, fL = 40 Hz and fH = 20 kHz. Find the bandwidth and the gain at the cut-off frequencies (as a number and in dB).

say.en: Let us work this out together. An amplifier has a mid-band gain of 120, fL equals 40 hertz and fH equals 20 kilohertz. Find the bandwidth and the gain at the cut-off frequencies as a number and in dB.
BW equals fH - fL equals 20 000 minus 40 equals 19 960 hertz is approximately 19.96 kilohertz.
Gain at cut-off equals 0.707 times 120 equals 84.9.
Mid-band gain equals 20 log 120 equals 41.6 dB, so the cut-off gain is 38.6 dB 3 dB less.
So the answer is BW is approximately 19.96 kilohertz; gain is approximately 84.9 38.6 dB.

problem.en: A coupling capacitor of 10 µF feeds an amplifier whose input resistance is 1 kΩ. Estimate the lower cut-off frequency set by this RC pair.

steps.en: A larger coupling capacitor would lower fL further.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. A coupling capacitor of 10 µF feeds an amplifier whose input resistance is 1 kΩ. Estimate the lower cut-off frequency set by this RC pair.

say.en: Let us work this out together. A coupling capacitor of 10 microfarads feeds an amplifier whose input resistance is 1 k ohms. Estimate the lower cut-off frequency set by this RC pair.
For one RC pair, fL equals 1 over 2 pi RC.
fL equals 1 over (2 pi times 1000 times 10 times 10 to the power minus 6) equals 15.9 hertz.
A larger coupling capacitor would lower fL further.
So the answer is fL is approximately 16 hertz.
